For example, if a draftsperson's base rate is $30 per hour, the casual rate would be $37.50 per hour. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Draftsperson Salary

Whether you're negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. For a **draftsperson salary**, the most common assumption is a 38-hour week and a 52-week year. This article walks you through the formula, explains the role of awards and the National Minimum Wage, and shows how tax and super fit in.

## The 38-Hour Week and the 52-Week Year

Most full-time employees in Australia work a 38-hour week, as set by modern awards and the Fair Work Act. When converting an hourly rate to annual pay, we multiply by hours per week and then by 52 weeks. This gives a standard annual figure before any overtime, penalties, or allowances.

For a draftsperson covered by an award like the Manufacturing Award, the 38-hour week is the baseline. If you work part-time or casual, your hours may differ, but the same formula applies – just use your actual weekly hours.

## From Hourly to Annual: The Formula

The core calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, if your draftsperson salary is $35 per hour:

$35 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $69,160 per year

This is your gross pay before tax and before super is added. The same formula works for any hourly rate. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to try different numbers.

## The Fortnight Perspective

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay:

**Weekly pay = hourly rate × 38 hours**
**Fortnightly pay = weekly pay × 2**

Using the $35/hour example:

Weekly = $1,330
Fortnightly = $2,660

This can help you budget and compare salary offers that are quoted annually or fortnightly.

## National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for employees aged 21 and over. However, most draftspersons are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, including the Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award 2020, which covers many draftspersons.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For a draftsperson on $30/hour base, the casual rate is $37.50/hour. Our [the timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

Award rates also include penalty rates for evening, weekend, or public holiday work. These are not included in the simple hourly-to-annual conversion, but they can significantly increase actual earnings.

## Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $69,160 annual salary, super would be approximately $8,299 per year, paid by your employer.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2%. For a $69,160 annual salary, the estimated tax (including Medicare) is about $11,667, leaving a take-home of around $57,493 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed breakdown.

## Using Our Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. The results include estimated tax and super, but remember these are estimates. They assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

For a draftsperson salary, you can also check the [reference tables](/data) for award-specific rates and allowances. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database provides the official minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award.

## Conclusion

Converting your draftsperson salary from hourly to annual is simple with the 38-hour week, 52-week year formula. Remember to factor in casual loading if applicable, and always check the relevant award for your minimum entitlements. Use our tools to estimate your take-home pay and super, and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) for the most accurate rates.
